name: Advanced Grants & AI
goal: Extend the working grant core with AI assistance and additional grant models (in-kind, tendered, multi-project) while people keep every decision.

features.name: AI assistance
features.summary: AI saves time on application forms, document checks and evaluation, and answers questions on grant data, while people confirm every value and take every decision.
features.decision: Which AI provider, and what data may be sent to it?

use_case.trigger: A user asks the AI for help (pre-fill, check, question), or the evaluation agent sends a report for an application.
preconditions: The AI service is configured for the Foundation.
The user's role is allowed to use the AI feature concerned.
main_flow: The charity user uploads a document on the application form and selects 'Fill with AI'; the system shows proposed values marked as AI-proposed.
The charity user reviews, edits and confirms; only confirmed values are saved.
On each uploaded attachment, the system runs an advisory AI check and shows a verdict and issues.
The External AI Evaluation Agent sends an evaluation report (score, criteria, summary, recommendation) for an application; the system validates and stores it.
The reviewer reads the AI evaluation in the dossier and records their own opinion; a contradicting opinion needs a justification.
A staff user asks the AI assistant a question; it answers from data the user may access and proposes links to pages where any action is confirmed.
alternative_flows: If the AI service fails or times out, then the system shows 'Could not get a response' and the user continues manually.
If an evaluation report is invalid or for an unknown application, then it is rejected with the list of problems.
business_rules: AI output is advisory: nothing is saved, approved or blocked by AI without a person's action.
The AI assistant is read-only and uses only the user's organization data within their permissions, decided by the system.
Evaluation reports are accepted only from an authenticated agent of the same Foundation; overall score 0–100, criterion scores 0–10 (max 50 criteria).
AI evaluation results are visible to grants staff only, never to charities.
Every AI request and received report is logged (user or agent, time, application or data area).

stories.title: AI pre-fill of application forms
stories.story: As a Charity user, I want AI to propose form values from my uploaded documents, so that I fill the application faster.
acceptance: Given I upload a document and select 'Fill with AI', then proposed values appear in the form marked as AI-proposed.
Given I leave the form without confirming, then no proposed value is saved.
Given I edit a proposed value and confirm, then my edited value is saved.

stories.title: Advisory AI document check
stories.story: As a Reviewer, I want an AI check on each attachment, so that I spot wrong or weak documents early.
acceptance: Given an attachment is uploaded, then the dossier shows the AI verdict (OK / Flagged) with the issues found.
Given a document is flagged, then the user can still submit or approve, after a confirmation prompt.
Given the AI check is unavailable, then the attachment is accepted and marked 'Not checked'.

stories.title: Receive external AI evaluation reports
stories.story: As a Grants Manager, I want the external evaluation agent to post its report on an application, so that reviewers get a structured AI evaluation.
acceptance: Given a report with valid agent credentials and a known application reference, then it is stored with the time received and logged in the application history.
Given an overall score of 120 or a criterion score of 11, then the report is rejected with the list of problems.
Given invalid credentials or an application of another Foundation, then the report is rejected.
stories.notes: Fields: score 0–100, colour band, label (≤80 chars), summary (≤2,000), recommendation (≤200), criterion scores.

stories.title: Use the AI evaluation in review
stories.story: As a Reviewer, I want to read the AI evaluation and record my own opinion, so that AI informs but does not replace my judgement.
acceptance: Given an application with an AI evaluation, then the dossier shows score, label, recommendation, summary and per-criterion scores; the charity never sees them.
Given my opinion contradicts the AI recommendation, when I save without a justification, then the system refuses.
Given one or more reviewers decided against the AI recommendation, then the decision-maker sees a warning with the count.

stories.title: AI assistant for grant questions
stories.story: As a Grants Manager, I want to ask questions about grant data in Arabic, so that I get answers without building reports.
acceptance: Given I ask 'Which payments are due this month?', then the answer lists figures from actual data in SAR with Western digits.
Given data outside my permissions, then the assistant does not use or reveal it.
Given a change is needed, then the assistant shows a link to the page where I confirm it; it never changes records itself.
Given any request, then it is logged with user, time, question and data areas read.
stories.notes: Charity users have no access to the assistant.

features.name: In-kind grants
features.summary: The Foundation can grant products from its own stock, not only money: products are offered through product opportunities, charities request quantities, approval deducts stock and delivery is recorded.

use_case.trigger: The Foundation wants to grant products from its catalog.
preconditions: The product catalog exists with stock.
main_flow: The Grants Manager maintains the product catalog: name, description, unit, unit price and stock.
The Grants Manager creates a product opportunity and ticks the catalog products offered.
The charity user submits a product request with quantities per product.
The request is reviewed and scored like other applications.
At final approval the system checks stock, deducts the approved quantities and sets the grant to Awaiting delivery.
After handover, the Grants Manager records the delivered quantities; the grant becomes Delivered.
alternative_flows: If a requested quantity exceeds available stock, then the request is refused naming the product and available quantity.
If stock is insufficient at final approval, then approval is blocked.
business_rules: Product name and unit are mandatory; unit price and stock are zero or more.
Each product appears at most once per opportunity.
Stock is deducted once, at final approval, and never becomes negative.
A product referenced by any request cannot be deleted, only archived.
In-kind grants do not create contracts or payments.

stories.title: Maintain the product catalog
stories.story: As a Grants Manager, I want to manage products with unit, price and stock, so that we know what we can grant.
acceptance: Given I add a product without a name, then the system refuses with 'Product name is required'.
Given a product referenced by a request, when I try to delete it, then the system offers only Archive.
Given the catalog, then each product shows name, unit, unit price and current stock.
stories.notes: Units: unit, device, basket, session, month, kilo, book, licence.

stories.title: Offer products in an opportunity
stories.story: As a Grants Manager, I want to select catalog products for a product opportunity, so that charities can request them.
acceptance: Given a product opportunity, when I tick products, then they are offered with unit price and available stock.
Given a product already on the opportunity, then it cannot be added twice.

stories.title: Request products
stories.story: As a Charity user, I want to request quantities of offered products, so that I receive goods for my beneficiaries.
acceptance: Given I request 50 units of a product with 30 in stock, then the request is refused with 'Requested quantity of <product> exceeds available (30)'.
Given I submit without any product quantity, then the system refuses with 'Select at least one product and quantity'.
Given a valid request, then it enters review with total value = Σ quantity × unit price.

stories.title: Approve and deliver an in-kind grant
stories.story: As a Grants Manager, I want approval to deduct stock and to record delivery, so that stock is accurate and delivery is tracked.
acceptance: Given final approval of 20 units with 30 in stock, then stock becomes 10 and the grant is Awaiting delivery.
Given stock fell below the approved quantity, then final approval is blocked with the product name and available quantity.
Given a grant Awaiting delivery, when I record delivered quantities, then it becomes Delivered and the history records the delivery; stock is not deducted again.
Given an approved in-kind grant, then no contract transfer is offered.

features.name: Tendered projects (RFP)
features.summary: The Foundation can tender a defined project, receive offers from invited charities, compare them side by side and award the best evaluated offer, which then becomes a contract and project.

use_case.trigger: The Foundation wants a defined project delivered by the best charity offer.
preconditions: An RFP opportunity with a budget ceiling exists.
main_flow: The Grants Manager enters scope of work, deliverables, duration, weighted activities and payment milestones (% of winning amount, days after award).
The system checks activity weights and payment percentages each total 100% and publishes the details to invited charities.
Invited charities submit technical and financial offers.
Reviewers evaluate offers against the criteria and pass score.
The Grants Manager compares offers side by side and selects 'Award' on one evaluated, passing offer.
The system awards it, closes all other offers with a notice, and creates the contract and project with activities and payments.
alternative_flows: If an offer exceeds the budget ceiling, then it is refused on submission.
If the award fails, then nothing is awarded or created.
business_rules: Activity weights and payment percentages must each total 100%.
The opportunity budget is the financial ceiling for offers.
Only one offer per RFP can be awarded, and only a pending offer that was evaluated and passed.
Payments = milestone % × winning amount; due dates counted from the award date.
The award is all-or-nothing.

stories.title: Define the tendered project
stories.story: As a Grants Manager, I want to define the scope, deliverables, activities and payment milestones of a tender, so that charities bid on the same requirements.
acceptance: Given activity weights totalling 95%, when I save, then the system refuses with 'Activity weights must total 100%'.
Given payment percentages totalling 110%, then the system refuses with 'Payment percentages must total 100%'.
Given valid details, then invited charities see them in the portal.

stories.title: Submit an offer
stories.story: As a Charity user, I want to submit a technical and financial offer to an RFP I am invited to, so that I can compete for the project.
acceptance: Given a budget ceiling of SAR 500,000, when I submit a financial offer of SAR 520,000, then it is refused with 'Financial offer exceeds the ceiling (500,000)'.
Given I am not invited, then I cannot see or bid on the RFP.
Given a valid offer, then it appears to staff with status Pending.

stories.title: Compare offers
stories.story: As a Grants Manager, I want to see offers side by side, so that I can choose the best value.
acceptance: Given several offers, then each card shows charity, financial offer, average evaluation score against the pass score and status, and the lowest financial offer is marked.
Given an offer not yet evaluated, then it shows 'Not evaluated' and cannot be awarded.

stories.title: Award the RFP
stories.story: As a Grants Manager, I want to award the best evaluated offer, so that the project starts with the winning charity.
acceptance: Given an offer below the pass score, then Award is not available.
Given I award a passing offer of SAR 450,000 with milestones 30%/70%, then a contract and project of SAR 450,000 are created with payments of SAR 135,000 and 315,000.
Given an award, then all other offers are closed as Not awarded and their charities receive the notice 'Thank you for your interest; the project was awarded to another offer'.
Given an RFP already awarded, then no second award is possible.

features.name: Multi-project grants, merges and funding conditions
features.summary: Complex grants are handled without workarounds: one application can be split into several projects, applications of the same charity can be merged, co-funding conditions and indicators are tracked, and the Foundation can run internal initiatives.

use_case.trigger: A grant needs a non-standard structure (split, merge, co-funding, indicators) or the Foundation runs its own initiative.
preconditions: The application is not yet transferred (for split, merge, co-funding and indicators).
main_flow: The Grants Manager registers co-funders with their contribution as Confirmed or as an approval condition, attaching the donor's approval when received.
The Grants Manager links plan indicators to the application with a required quantity.
To merge, the Grants Manager selects pending or approved applications of the same charity and grant type; the system shows the impact and builds one merged application.
At transfer, the Grants Manager chooses Split and assigns each cost item to a named project; each project's budget is the sum of its items.
The system creates one contract and the projects, carrying co-funding and indicators over.
Separately, the Grants Manager creates an internal initiative run by the Foundation, in Planning status.
alternative_flows: If a co-funding condition is unconfirmed, then final approval and transfer are blocked.
If the contract is still Being prepared, then a merge can be undone, restoring every original application.
business_rules: Split projects' budgets total the approved amount; split needs ≥2 cost items and every project ≥1 item.
Merging is allowed only for applications of the same charity and grant type, not transferred and not already merged; merged applications produce one contract.
A co-funding condition becomes confirmed only with the donor's approval evidence attached.
An indicator cannot be linked beyond its remaining target across all applications and projects.
Internal initiatives need a name, a budget > 0 and an end date not before the start date.

stories.title: Split an application into several projects
stories.story: As a Grants Manager, I want to split an approved application into several projects, so that distinct components are managed separately.
acceptance: Given an application with one cost item, then the Split option is not available.
Given a project in split mode has no cost item, then confirmation is disabled with 'Each project needs at least one item'.
Given a split of SAR 300,000 into two projects, then one contract of SAR 300,000 and two projects whose budgets total SAR 300,000 are created.

stories.title: Merge applications of the same charity
stories.story: As a Grants Manager, I want to merge several applications of one charity, so that they are decided and contracted as one grant.
acceptance: Given applications of different charities, then the merge is refused with 'Applications belong to different charities'.
Given a valid merge, then one merged application with the total amount is created and the absorbed applications are closed with 'Merged into <ref>'.
Given the merge would move a finally approved application back into review, then a second confirmation is required.
Given the merged application's contract has moved past Being prepared, then unmerge is not available.

stories.title: Co-funding conditions
stories.story: As a Grants Manager, I want to record co-funders and their approval conditions, so that we do not approve a grant whose co-funding is not secured.
acceptance: Given a co-funder without a name or with amount 0, then the system refuses with 'Enter donor name and amount'.
Given a co-funding condition without the donor's approval attached, when final approval is attempted, then it is blocked.
Given I attach the donor's approval, then the condition becomes Confirmed and is logged in the history.

stories.title: Link plan indicators
stories.story: As a Grants Manager, I want to link plan indicators with target quantities to an application, so that grant results roll up to the plan.
acceptance: Given an indicator with 40 remaining, when I link 50, then the system refuses with 'Only 40 remain for this indicator'.
Given the application is transferred, then indicators can no longer be changed from the application and are carried to the project(s).
stories.notes: Milestone-type indicators are linked with a target of 1.

stories.title: Create an internal initiative
stories.story: As a Grants Manager, I want to create an initiative run by the Foundation, so that internal work is followed like grant projects.
acceptance: Given a name and a budget of SAR 80,000, when I save, then the initiative is created in Planning with me as project manager by default and appears in the projects list as source Initiative.
Given a budget of 0 or an end date before the start date, then the system refuses with the specific error.
stories.notes: Executor can be internal or a registered charity.
